topics.title: Section A: Reading information and ideas

outcomes.text: Identify and interpret key ideas and information in unseen 19th and 20th/21st century non-fiction texts.
Read in different ways for different purposes, analysing texts that persuade, inform, instruct or advise.
Summarise ideas from one text and synthesise information from more than one text.
Comment on writers' choices of vocabulary, form and grammatical features, attending to detail.
Explore the effects of writing for particular audiences and purposes.
Use linguistic terminology accurately to support analysis.
Draw inferences and justify points of view with close reference to evidence from the text.
Evaluate a text's usefulness by spotting bias and misuse of evidence.
Compare how effectively texts achieve their purposes, judging usefulness, relevance and presentation.
Use understanding of a text's context, such as its historical setting or genre, to inform reading.
Explore connections across texts to understand the ideas, attitudes and values presented.

topics.title: Section B: Writing for audience, impact and purpose

outcomes.text: Write original non-fiction (articles, speeches, letters) to describe, explain, inform, instruct, argue or persuade.
Adapt tone, style and register for different audiences, purposes and contexts.
Use information provided by others to write in different forms.
Organise ideas and information clearly and coherently.
Select and emphasise key ideas to influence readers and fit the purpose.
Maintain a consistent viewpoint across a piece of non-fiction.
Make considered vocabulary and grammar choices for particular audiences and purposes.
Use rhetorical devices and techniques learned from wide reading of non-fiction.
Cite evidence and quotation effectively to support views.
Write to create emotional impact.
Use a range of sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate punctuation and spelling.

topics.title: Section A: Reading meaning and effects

outcomes.text: Comment on writers' choices of vocabulary, form and grammatical features and how they create meaning in unseen 20th/21st century prose.
Analyse and compare writers' use of language, attending to detail.
Use linguistic and literary terminology to support analysis.
Draw inferences and justify points of view with close reference to the text.
Interpret writers' meanings and effects in one text and across two texts.
Identify the main themes and ideas in texts.
Evaluate how form and structure add to a text's effectiveness and impact.
Use understanding of context, such as setting or genre, to inform reading.
Explore connections across texts to understand ideas, attitudes and values.

topics.title: Section B: Writing imaginatively and creatively

outcomes.text: Write original creative texts such as short stories and autobiographical pieces.
Organise and structure narrative ideas to create deliberate effects.
Maintain a consistent viewpoint, making conscious choices such as narrative point of view.
Make considered vocabulary and grammar choices to create deliberate effects.
Use language creatively and imaginatively, drawing on narrative techniques from wide reading of prose fiction and literary non-fiction.
Adapt tone, style and register as appropriate.
Select and emphasise key ideas to create meaning and influence readers.
Use a range of sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate punctuation and spelling.
